# Ephyra

> Ephyra is a free, open-source (GPLv3) Jellyfin client for Android phones, tablets and Android TV. It is a fork of Findroid and was called Findroid CE until version 2.0.0. It needs a Jellyfin server (12.0 or newer) and Android 10 or newer (Android 9 or newer on TV).

What Ephyra adds to Findroid:

- Downloads: resumable, to internal storage or an SD card, with a quality per download (the original, or a server conversion from 4K down to 360p), whole seasons or series at once, and opt-in Smart Downloads that keep the next episodes of what you are watching. Downloads play without a connection, with no offline mode to switch on.
- Cast: Google Cast (Chromecast) from phones and tablets, in the proprietary variant of the app. The libre variant has no Google code.
- Playback: Dolby Vision direct play where the device supports it, Dolby Atmos through the device's decoder, PGS, VobSub and DVB subtitles without transcoding, subtitle styling on ExoPlayer and mpv, a version picker, a quality switch during playback, and audio and subtitle choices remembered per series.
- Library: Home rows you choose and order, a hide-watched filter, opt-in ratings from IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic and Letterboxd through MDBList, and profiles that can be locked with a PIN.
- Tablets and foldables: a navigation rail, list-detail seasons, keyboard and mouse support in the player.
- Android TV: a separate app built for the remote, with trickplay thumbnails, refresh rate switching, the Watch Next row and a screensaver. It has builds for 64-bit devices and for 32-bit boxes such as the Xiaomi Mi Box.

Ephyra collects nothing. It talks to the Jellyfin servers the user adds, and to MDBList only when the user switches on external ratings with their own key.

## Links

- [Website](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/): features, screenshots and install instructions
- [Guide](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/guide/): how to install and use Ephyra, with every feature per area
- [Install](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/guide/install/): Obtainium, the releases page, the stores, and which file is for which device
- [What runs where](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/guide/devices/): every feature and whether the phone, the tablet and the TV app have it
- [Ephyra and Findroid](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/guide/findroid/): what happens with Findroid's changes, and moving over from Findroid or Findroid CE
- [Developing Ephyra](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/dev/): the architecture, the areas of the code and the decision records
- [Source code](https://github.com/midasvo/ephyra)
- [Releases](https://github.com/midasvo/ephyra/releases): APK downloads for phone, tablet and Android TV
- [Beta](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/guide/beta/): a prerelease of every change, installed next to the stable app
- [Changelog](https://github.com/midasvo/ephyra/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- [Issues](https://github.com/midasvo/ephyra/issues): bug reports and requests
- [Privacy policy](https://midasvo.nl/ephyra/privacy.html)
- [Findroid](https://github.com/jarnedemeulemeester/findroid): the app Ephyra is forked from
- [libmpv for Android](https://midasvo.nl/libmpv-android/): Ephyra's own build of mpv and FFmpeg, used by its mpv player
